text:
Predicates:
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
Win(x, y) ::: x wins in y.
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: x is named after y.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Nemesis(x, y) ::: y is the nemesis of x.
Appear(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
MovieCharacter(x, y) ::: x is a character in movie y.
BadGuy(x) ::: x is a bad guy.
Premises:
∀m (SuperheroMovie(m) → ∀x (GoodGuy(x) → Win(x, m))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y ((GoodGuy(x) ∧ BadGuy(y)) → (Fight(x, y) ∧ Fight(y, x))) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesisOfSirDigby) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀m ∀c (SuperheroMovie(m) ∧ NamedAfter(m, c) → GoodGuy(c)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Win(x, y) → ∀z (Fight(x, z) → ¬Win(z, y))) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
∀m ∀c (SuperheroMovie(m) ∧ NamedAfter(m, c) → Appear(c, m)) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
¬Win(nemesisOfSirDigby, surprisingAdventures) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
